title: Standardize 3D camera and projection logic across modules
body:
Currently, 3D visualization modules (such as the Bloch sphere and Lorenz attractor) independently implement their own manual projection and rotation logic. This fragmentation has resulted in inconsistent coordinate systems, varying navigation behaviors, and redundant math code across the codebase. 

This Pull Request introduces a centralized **3D Tool Framework** to unify the spatial experience and simplify the development of future 3D modules.

### Key Changes

- **Core `Camera3D` Abstraction**: Moved projection, pitch, yaw, and zoom logic from individual tabs into a reusable `Camera3D` struct within the framework. This ensures that the math for orthographic projection is calculated identically everywhere.
- **Unified Coordinate System**: Enforced a **Z-up** orientation across all 3D viewports. Previously, some modules like the `AttractorPlotter` relied on Y-up, which caused orientation conflicts when switching between tools.
- **Direct Manipulation Controls**: Integrated `handle_interaction` directly into the camera framework. This provides out-of-the-box support for:
    - **Drag-to-rotate**: Intuitive pitch and yaw control.
    - **Scroll-to-zoom**: Standardized focal length adjustment.
- **State Synchronization**: Implemented logic to ensure that camera changes triggered by mouse interactions are reflected in the side-panel UI sliders, preventing state drift between the viewport and the control panel.
- **Module Refactoring**: Updated `AttractorPlotter`, `SurfaceViewer`, and `SpinVisualizer` to use the new framework, successfully removing duplicated array manipulation and projection logic from these files.

### Rationale

The primary goal is to improve **user intuition**. By standardizing the "spatial grammar" of the application, users no longer need to relearn how to navigate when switching between different mathematical visualizations. 

From a development perspective, this abstraction reduces the barrier to entry for new modules. Researchers can now focus on defining 3D coordinates for their specific domain (e.g., topology or physics) without worrying about the underlying camera matrix or input handling.

### Performance & Compatibility
- **2D Modules**: Existing 2D-only modules (like Fractals) remain untouched and are unaffected by these changes.
- **Optimization**: The abstraction layer maintains real-time performance for high-density surfaces by utilizing shared math utilities instead of expensive high-level overhead.

### Acceptance Criteria Verified
- [x] Redundant projection logic removed from individual tool files.
- [x] Mouse-drag rotation active in all 3D modules.
- [x] Identical "Up" axis across all tabs.
- [x] Side-panel sliders stay in sync with manual viewport rotations.
